SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL P
C. I. D. REGIST
No. 1. O. D. 1357.
Date..16....6...30.

June 16, 30.

Sir,

I have the honour to refer to your letter,
No. 800B COS:NLH, dated June 6, 1930, and to inform
you that Charles "Sunset" Cox has resided at the
Savoy Hotel, Broadway, since June 1929. He has
spent many years in the East and, prior to residing
in Shanghai, lived in the Philippine Islands where
he was, for a considerable time, on the staff of
the "Manila Bulletin". At present he writes articles
for the "China Press", but is not employed in a
permanent capacity.

It would appear that Cox is an educated
man who is more familiar with other circumstances
than those under which he is living at present.
His sister, the wife of Mr. Frank Vanderlip, a
wealthy American financier, until recently contributed
towards his support. He is believed to be in
receipt of a small pension from the American
Government for former military service. This,
together with the money he receives from the articles
accepted by the "China Press", is chiefly expended
in drink.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your Obedient Servant,
Deputy Commissioner -
(Crime & Special Branches).

Edwin S. Cunningham Esq.,
American Consul-General,
Shanghai.

上海公共租界工部局警务处
刑事侦缉处登记簿
编号：I. O. D. 1357.
日期..1930....6...16...

1930年6月16日。

先生：

谨此回复阁下1930年6月6日第800B COS:NLH号来函，并告知查尔斯·“日落”·考克斯（Charles "Sunset" Cox）自1929年6月起一直居住于百老汇路的萨伏伊酒店（Savoy Hotel）。他在东方生活多年，在移居上海之前，曾居住在菲律宾群岛，并在相当长的一段时间内任职于《马尼拉公报》（Manila Bulletin）编辑部。目前他为《字林西报》（China Press）撰写文章，但并非该报的正式雇员。

考克斯似乎是一位受过教育的人士，对他目前所处环境之外的其他境况更为熟悉。他的姐姐是美国富有的金融家弗兰克·范德利普（Frank Vanderlip）先生的夫人，据悉直至最近一直在资助他的生活。据信，他因曾在美军服役而从美国政府领取少量养老金。这笔钱加上他从《字林西报》录用文章中获得的稿酬，主要都花费在饮酒上。

谨此致意，
先生，
您顺从的仆人，
副总监 -
（刑事及特务科）。

致：
埃德温·S·坎宁安先生（Edwin S. Cunningham Esq.），
美国驻上海总领事，
上海。

Special Branch
No. 2.
(C. & S.B.) Office Notes

File No. 10 D 1360
June 13, 1930.

Sir,

Reference the attached letter from the American
Consul General.

Charles "Sunset" Cox has been residing at
the Savoy Hotel, Broadway, since June 1929. He
has spent many years in the East and previous to
taking up residence in Shanghai, lived in the
Phillipine Islands and was for some considerable
time on the staff of the "Manila Bulletin." At
present he writes articles for the "China Press,"
but is not employed by that paper in a permanent
capacity.

He appears to be a man of some education who
has come down in the world and is more familiar
with other circumstances than those under which he
is at present living. His sister, the wife of
Mr. Frank Vanderlip, a wealthy American financier,
it is understood, until recently contributed towards
his support.

He is believed to be in receipt of a small
pension from the American Government for former
military service. This along with money he receives
from the articles accepted by the "China Press"
is chiefly expended in drink.

W. Moore.
D. F. S.

D. C.
(C. & S. Branches)

Reg. Please draft reply to U. S. Consul's
letter giving the above information.
14/6/30.

（左侧手写批注：Wh 13. 6. 30.）

他似乎是一位受过一定教育但家道中落的人士，对他目前所处环境之外的其他境况更为熟悉。据悉，他的姐姐是美国富有的金融家弗兰克·范德利普先生的夫人，直至最近一直在资助他的生活。

据信，他因曾在美军服役而从美国政府领取少量养老金。这笔钱加上他从《字林西报》录用文章中获得的稿酬，主要都花费在饮酒上。

W. 摩尔（W. Moore）。
副特别警司（D. F. S.）。

副总监（D. C.）
（刑事及特务科）

注册。请草拟回复美国领事的信函，提供上述信息。
